title: Aaron Judge to undergo additional testing as Yankees wait for word on his injury
content:
NEW YORK — The New York Yankees are still awaiting word on whether Aaron Judge will require a stint on the injured list while he deals with a bone bruise on his upper right rib that has forced him to miss two games.

Manager Aaron Boone told reporters after the Yankees’ 5-4 loss to the Cleveland Guardians on Wednesday that Judge requires more imaging after undergoing tests earlier in the afternoon.

“The specialist got back to us, confirmed what we’ve seen to this point,” Boone said. “They just want to get some more specific spots.”

Boone said the additional tests are “more high-power, more specific,” allowing the specialist to view the rib and chest area from different angles. When specifically asked whether a fracture has been ruled out by the initial testing, Boone could not give a direct answer.

“I don’t want to speak out of turn. I don’t know that yet,” Boone said. “It’s to a point where he’s not playing. We just want to make sure that we get a really strong diagnosis of things, and hopefully then we can roll.”

Boone said earlier this week that Judge had been nursing the injury for weeks, but his condition had worsened over the weekend in the series against the Athletics in Sacramento and had probably been affecting him at the plate for a while. Since May 17, Judge has hit .163 with one home run and eight RBIs over 13 games.

“I think there’s at least some correlation, whether it’s every day in those couple of weeks,” Boone said Wednesday afternoon.

José Caballero has played right field in Judge’s absence the past two games despite not getting any reps there this season. Boone announced before Wednesday’s game that Jasson Domínguez will begin a rehab assignment on Friday. If Judge needs to miss time, the Yankees could recall Domínguez when he’s fully healthy and move Cody Bellinger to right field. That would then force Boone to decide between Caballero and Anthony Volpe at shortstop.

Even before Judge started dealing with the effects of his rib injury, he had not been performing at the Ruthian standard he’s established for himself. Judge’s .908 OPS is 13th-best in MLB; the three-time MVP has not finished lower than No. 1 in OPS since 2021 in every season he has qualified for the batting title.

A lengthy Judge absence may not be as devastating for the Yankees’ hopes as it was for the team in 2023, when the star crashed into Dodger Stadium’s wall and broke his right big toe. That injury effectively ended the Yankees’ season. The team has more offensive depth this year than it did then.

“Judge is great and everything, but he (can’t) do it by himself,” second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. said.
